findings.claim: A 20-mark extended response must address both performer choices and design discipline choices.
findings.truth: In Section B, the 20-mark part offers a choice between a performer response and one design specialism. The response must follow the perspective and requirements in the question.
findings.evidence: AQA GCSE Drama 8261 specification, 4.2 Assessment components; AQA June 2023 written paper.

findings.claim: A 20-mark staging question requires at least three design disciplines and a named performer choice.
findings.truth: The 20-mark Section B part is answered as either a performer or a designer. Students should meet the perspective and requirements stated in that question.
findings.evidence: AQA GCSE Drama 8261 specification, 4.2 Assessment components; AQA June 2023 written paper.

findings.claim: The fixed exam format is an 8-mark designer question followed by a 20-mark response combining design and performance.
findings.truth: AQA's set-text question sequence is 4, 8, 12 and 20 marks. The 2023 8-mark item was a performer task, while the 20-mark item offered performer or designer routes.
findings.evidence: AQA GCSE Drama 8261 assessment information; AQA June 2023 written paper.

findings.claim: Abdul arrives with no English and develops his English later in the play.
findings.truth: Abdul speaks English when he appears in the published play text; performance suggestions must not present English as a skill he acquires during the plot.
findings.evidence: Tanika Gupta, The Empress, published text: Abdul speaks English in the opening voyage/docks material.

findings.claim: Examiners ask students to discuss practitioner influence on a set play.
findings.truth: The specification requires practical exploration and set-text knowledge, but does not prescribe a practitioner-influence question for the set-play assessment. Practitioner application can be presented as an interpretive approach.
findings.evidence: AQA GCSE Drama 8261 specification, 3.1 Understanding drama and 4.2 Assessment components.

findings.claim: An 8-mark performer response without both a vocal and physical choice is capped at Secure.
findings.truth: AQA's 8-mark performer task asks for vocal and physical skills, but the stated house ceiling is not a specification rule. Advise students to use both skills without claiming a fixed cap.
findings.evidence: AQA November 2021 written paper and marking guidance; AQA GCSE Drama 8261 specification.

findings.claim: The Ayahs' Home in Hackney is the institution and setting used in the play's 1887–1891 action.
findings.truth: Option A (recommended): standardise the unit to the play's Home for Ayahs in Jewry Street, Aldgate, in 1891, and distinguish this from the move to Hackney in 1900. Option B: retain a different location only if the locally prescribed edition demonstrably changes the setting. This error recurs in lessons 1, 3, 4 and 6 and in linked practice, check and flashcard fields.
findings.evidence: RSC The Empress plot: Jewry Street, Aldgate, Home for Ayahs, 1891; English Heritage, The Ayahs' Home: move to 26 King Edward's Road, Hackney, on 1 January 1900.
findings.ruling: Unit needs a content rebuild against the published text: recurring wrong setting (Hackney vs Jewry Street 1891), Hari/Naoroji conflation, invented Mrs Wormwood (Mrs Matthews), invented methods (direct address, Abdul letters), Brecht/Stanislavski attribution, fixed 12-mark intentions framing. Not fixable by surgical edits across 8 lessons; queue status set to needs-rebuild for Tom.

findings.claim: Hari Mohan Lal is a composite political figure inspired by Dadabhai Naoroji.
findings.truth: Option A (recommended): distinguish Hari, the fictional lascar, from Dadabhai Naoroji, the historical politician who appears in the play. Option B: retain a composite-character claim only with a source for a different adaptation. The conflation recurs in lessons 2, 3 and 7 and in related checks and flashcards.
findings.evidence: RSC The Empress characters and plot: Hari is a lascar; Dadabhai Naoroji is separately listed. UK Parliament: Naoroji was elected Liberal MP for Finsbury Central in 1892.
